newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian govt unaware Svyazinvest investment plans.
newsitem.headline: Russian govt unaware Svyazinvest investment plans.

text.p: The Russian government, four days after its biggest privatisation yet, is in the dark about whether the winners will make any investments in telecoms holding company Svyazinvest, a senior minister said on Tuesday.
Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Bulgak told a news conference the terms of the tender for 25 percent plus one share in Svyazinvest did not specify any investment demands.
"Different buyers have different promises -- we have seen this during overall privatisation. Time will show how real these promises are," Bulgak said.
He said the contract for the $1.875 billion deal would probably be signed on Wednesday.

The winner of the auction was a financial consortium led by Russia's Uneximbank. It also comprises George Soros's Quantum fund, Germany's Deutsche Bank investment arm Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG), Morgan Stanley Asset Management and Moscow investment bank Renaissance Capital.
Earlier the head of DMG in Moscow, Nick Jordan, said the bank did not intend to sell its Svyazinvest shares quickly.

Analysts praised the auction as the most open sale so far raising the most money for the cash-strapped government, but said Svyazinvest would have gained if the winners had included a telecoms company.
Svyazinvest holds controlling stakes in 89 telecoms companies, including long-distance carrier Rostelekom.
The auction sparked an immediate rise in telecoms companies' share prices, with some stocks rising on Monday by 10 percent.
